title: Finite finitely presented envelope for a separated etale morphism
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A morphism is finite if representable and finite on all scheme tests [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Local finite presentation is tested on etale scheme charts [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; finite presentation additionally requires quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness, meaning a quasi-compact relative diagonal. Let $T$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated, where a quasi-compact space admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme and quasi-separated means that its absolute diagonal is quasi-compact. Let $f:W\to T$ be quasi-compact, separated and etale. Here quasi-compactness is tested after pullback to affine schemes, separated means that the relative diagonal is a representable closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and etale is tested on compatible etale scheme charts [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Then there are an algebraic space $Y$, a quasi-compact representable open immersion $j:W\hookrightarrow Y$ [def-weil-open-immersion], and a finite morphism of finite presentation $\pi:Y\to T$ such that $f=\pi\circ j$.

source.place: Tag 0874 (lemma-quasi-finite-separated-pass-through-finite-addendum), with Tag 082K (lemma-quasi-finite-separated-pass-through-finite); etale morphisms are locally of finite presentation and locally quasi-finite, so the quasi-compact etale case is included.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], applied to algebraic spaces viewed as discrete algebraic stacks, $f$ is locally of finite presentation, hence locally of finite type, and its arbitrary scheme base changes are chartwise etale. They remain separated by [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition]. For every scheme $B\to T$, [lem-a1-separated-etale-space-scheme] therefore represents $W\times_TB$ by a scheme etale over $B$. Consequently $f$ is representable; this uses separatedness, rather than assuming that every chartwise etale map is representable.

source.place: Tags 03XU (lemma-etale-locally-quasi-finite), 03XX (proposition-locally-quasi-finite-separated-over-scheme), 03KL (lemma-base-change-separated); chartwise base change: spaces-properties.tex Tag 03FU (lemma-base-change-etale).

proof.text: On each etale scheme chart of the target, the representing scheme morphism is etale, thus unramified by [def-weil-etale-morphism] and locally quasi-finite by [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-quasi-finite-at-points]. Hence $f$ is quasi-finite at every point in the precise chartwise sense used in [lem-sfb-space-normalization-quasifinite-locus]. Since it is quasi-compact and separated, take its relative normalization $W\xrightarrow{a}N\xrightarrow{n}T$ from [lem-sfb-space-relative-integral-factorization]. That universal property is exactly the normalization hypothesis of the locus lemma. Apply it to the representable finite-type separated $f$: its open isomorphism locus has inverse image all of $W$, so $a$ identifies $W$ with an open subspace of $N$. The integral morphism $n$ is affine and separated and $N$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-sfb-space-integral-qcqs-permanence]. Since $na=f$ is quasi-compact and $n$ is quasi-separated, [lem-sfb-space-qc-cancellation] makes $a$ quasi-compact.

Apply [lem-sfb-integral-space-finite-presentation-limit] to $n:N\to T$. Obtain a small nonempty directed inverse system $(N_i)$ over $T$, with affine transitions, each $N_i\to T$ finite and finitely presented and each $N_i$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, with limit $N$. The limit is also the fppf sheaf limit by [lem-sfb-space-affine-limits-schematic-stages]: its sheaf limit is an algebraic space, hence has the same universal property and is uniquely isomorphic to $N$. The open $W\subset N$ is quasi-compact as a space. Indeed $N$ is quasi-compact, so choose a surjective etale map $U\to N$ from a quasi-compact scheme. Since $a$ is quasi-compact on affine tests, [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests] makes its pullback $W\times_NU$ over the quasi-compact scheme $U$ a quasi-compact space. Composing a surjective etale map from a quasi-compact scheme onto $W\times_NU$ with the base change $W\times_NU\to W$ of $U\to N$, which is surjective and etale by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], gives a surjective etale map from a quasi-compact scheme onto $W$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-limit-open-cover-descent] to the two-member finite open cover $(W,N)$ of $N$. In particular it supplies some index $i$ and a quasi-compact open $V_i\subset N_i$ with $N\times_{N_i}V_i=W$. Including $N$ in the cover is necessary: the cited statement concerns a covering family, not an arbitrary single open.

source.place: Tags 09YA (lemma-integral-limit-finite-and-finite-presentation), 07SF (lemma-directed-inverse-system-has-limit), 0827 (lemma-descend-opens); the finite-stage construction in spaces-more-morphisms.tex Tag 082K. Quasi-compactness of W: spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03KG (lemma-quasi-compact-local).

proof.text: Restrict to the directed tail $k\ge i$ and put $V_k=N_k\times_{N_i}V_i$. [lem-sfb-space-limit-open-cover-descent] ensures that all $V_k$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated and their transitions are affine. By the base-change/limit identity of [lem-sfb-space-affine-limits-schematic-stages], their limit is $N\times_{N_i}V_i=W$, with the compatible maps induced by $a$. Use [lem-sfb-space-eventual-closed-immersion] with base $B=T$, inverse system $(V_k)$, and the identity closed immersion from $W$ to its limit. The source $W\to T$ is locally of finite type by step 1, and all stages are quasi-compact. Thus for some $k\ge i$ the projection $b:W\to V_k$ is a closed immersion. Fix this $k$ and write $C=N_k$, $V=V_k$, and $p:C\to T$.

source.place: Tags 07SF (lemma-directed-inverse-system-has-limit), 0828 (lemma-finite-type-eventually-closed), clause (1), applied as in spaces-more-morphisms.tex Tag 082K.

proof.text: The open inclusion $V\hookrightarrow C$ is quasi-compact: $V$ is quasi-compact and $C$ quasi-separated, so apply [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-permanence]. It is finitely presented by [lem-sfb-space-qc-open-finite-presentation]. Since $p$ is finitely presented, [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition] makes $V\to T$ finitely presented, hence locally of finite type by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Now $W\to T$ is locally of finite presentation (step 1); [lem-sfb-space-relative-lfp-permanence] applied to $W\xrightarrow{b}V\to T$ makes $b$ locally of finite presentation. Let $\mathcal I\subset\mathcal O_V$ be its quasi-coherent ideal, supplied by [lem-sfb-space-ideal-closed-subspace-correspondence]. The equivalence in [lem-sfb-space-closed-structure-finite-presentation] shows that $\mathcal I$ is of finite type.

Apply [lem-sfb-space-finite-type-submodule-extension] on the quasi-compact quasi-separated space $C$, its quasi-compact open $V$, and $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_C$, to $\mathcal I\subset\mathcal O_C|_V$. This gives a finite-type quasi-coherent submodule $\mathcal J\subset\mathcal O_C$ restricting exactly to $\mathcal I$. A submodule of the structure ring module is already an ideal: for local sections $r\in\mathcal O_C$ and $s\in\mathcal J$, the product $rs$ is the scalar action and lies in $\mathcal J$. By [lem-sfb-space-ideal-closed-subspace-correspondence] form $e:Y=V(\mathcal J)\hookrightarrow C$. Under the etale base change $V\hookrightarrow C$, its ideal is $\mathcal J|_V=\mathcal I$, so the same bijection identifies $Y\times_CV$ with the given closed subspace $b:W\hookrightarrow V$. The inclusion $j:W\to Y$ is therefore an open immersion, as can be checked on each scheme test by pulling back the open $V\subset C$. By construction $ej$ is the fixed map $W\to C$ from the inverse system.

source.place: Tag 0853 (lemma-extend), with F equal to the structure sheaf; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03MB (lemma-closed-immersion-ideals). This is the finite-type-ideal refinement of the immersion reversal used in Tag 082K.

proof.text: Because $\mathcal J$ is of finite type, [lem-sfb-space-closed-structure-finite-presentation] makes $e$ finitely presented. Set $\pi=pe:Y\to T$. It is finitely presented by [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition]. It is finite directly on scheme tests: for any affine test $H=\operatorname{Spec}R\to T$, $C_H=\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $A$ finite as an $R$-module, and the closed immersion $Y_H\hookrightarrow C_H$ has the form $\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}A$ by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The images of a finite set of $R$-module generators of $A$ generate $A/J$, proving finiteness by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Thus $\pi$ is affine and separated by [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality]. Since $\pi j=f$ is quasi-compact, [lem-sfb-space-qc-cancellation] makes $j$ quasi-compact. The equality $\pi j=f$ is the equality $p(ej)=f$ of the compatible $T$-maps fixed in steps 3-6. This gives every required clause, without requiring $Y\to T$ to be etale.
